# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 74 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 74

He said: "Lord, there are many around the drinking-trough, but there is nothing in the well."

---

**Council Notes:**

- One of the most enigmatic sayings in Thomas. The crowd gathers at the watering-place but the source is empty.
- Interpretations: (1) Many follow religion outwardly but find no inner substance. (2) The crowd seeks Jesus but is not spiritually prepared to receive him. (3) There are many seeking but few true finders (cf. Saying 2).
- "Drinking-trough" (EMET) preserved over "cistern" (LOGOS) — emphasizes the gathering-to-drink function. PNEUMA's "watering-place" is acceptable but loses the vessel specificity.
- "Nothing in the well" vs. "the well is empty" (PNEUMA): "nothing in" preserves the literal Coptic construction; "empty" is interpretively equivalent.
